subject.title: feat(computer-use): control macOS nodes via screenshots and input injection

question: Should OpenClaw ship this bundled macOS node computer-use executor now, and what live-proof/security gate is required before merge?
rationale: The patch introduces model-driven screenshots plus real mouse and keyboard injection through a new plugin/node boundary, and automation cannot decide the intended security and release gate without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fix and prove before merge
options.body: Require the plus-key fix, accepted manifest-contract base, and redacted real Mac proof showing setting, TCC, allowlist or approval, and a successful pointer/key action before merge.

options.title: Pause for contract redesign
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers settle a narrower or external plugin-host boundary for Computer Use provider ownership and macOS permission binding.

options.title: Accept the proof gap
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally land with only mocked/unit evidence, but that accepts unproven CoreGraphics/TCC behavior on a security-sensitive feature.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove before merge
recommendation.body: Require the plus-key fix, accepted manifest-contract base, and redacted real Mac proof showing setting, TCC, allowlist or approval, and a successful pointer/key action before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-main and PR-stack history across the macOS node and dangerous node-command policy surfaces involved in the decision.
